headline: Bitcoin is holding just under $80,000 ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision, in a week packed with crypto company earnings and a big Friday options expiry.

market.asOf: BTC, ETH and SOL from the Motley Fool's market report at 5:25pm ET Mon 26 Oct (21:25 UTC; 04:25 Tue Bangkok); the price sites could not be reached this run. The Fear & Greed index was not read this run. Live prices are at the top of the page.

stories.title: Bitcoin slips just under $80,000 into a busy Fed, earnings and options week
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell below $80,000 on Monday as traders cut risk before Wednesday's Fed decision. Money left the US spot bitcoin funds late last week, and spot ether funds lost money for the week. A large batch of bitcoin options expires on Friday.
points: Bitcoin's Monday low was just under $79,300, per Quartz.
At 5:25pm ET Monday bitcoin was $79,817, down 0.28% on the day and 2.4% over 7 days; ether was $2,313.61, down 3.5% over 7 days, per the Motley Fool.

Spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold bitcoin for stock-market investors) lost $635.6M on 22 Oct and $137.9M on 23 Oct but ended the week $301.2M positive, per Farside. Monday's flows were not posted yet.
Spot ether ETFs lost $220.7M over 19-23 Oct, per Farside.
The Fed decides on Wednesday; Polymarket priced a 94.5% chance of no change, per Coinspeaker.

stories.title: A rough security week: Electrum wallet bug, CoinDCX's $16M loss and two DeFi exploits
stories.summary: A bug in the Electrum bitcoin wallet let rogue servers trick users into paying an attacker when they tried to speed up a payment; version 4.8.3 fixes it. India's CoinDCX admitted a $16M loss after first calling reports a false alarm. Two DeFi projects, X100 and Initia, were also exploited.
points: In Electrum, a rogue server could show a fake pending payment; if the user pressed 'speed up', the wallet signed a new payment to the attacker. Version 4.8.3, released 24 Oct, fixes it, per CoinDesk.
Electrum users should update, use trusted servers and check the full receiving address, since attackers used addresses matching the last 4 characters, per CoinDesk.
CoinDCX lost 15.99M USDT (about $16M) tied to a retired wallet; it says customer balances were not affected and it absorbed the loss, per CoinDesk.
X100 lost about $4.75M in a flash-loan governance attack on 24 Oct (PeckShield figure), and the attacker moved 821.2 ETH into Tornado Cash, per The Crypto Times.
Initia's chain has been halted since 23 Oct after a bug let an attacker mint 2M unbacked AUSD and take about $2.7M, per Altcoin Buzz.

sources.label: The Crypto Times: X100 exploiter moves 821 ETH

stories.title: US regulators move on crypto while Congress stalls: CFTC exchange path, OCC stablecoin push, NBA deal
stories.summary: With the market-structure bill stuck in the Senate, US regulators are acting on their own. The CFTC is working on a voluntary federal registration path for crypto exchanges, the bank regulator is urging community banks to issue stablecoins, and the NBA signed an integrity deal with the CFTC and named Kalshi and Polymarket as partners.
points: The CFTC's voluntary registration path would cover exchanges offering retail customers leveraged or margined crypto trading; it is an early-stage proposal with comments due 14 Dec, per crypto.news.
The CLARITY Act market-structure bill failed a Senate procedural vote 49-50 on 15 Sep, per crypto.news.
The OCC is urging community banks to apply to issue payment stablecoins under the GENIUS Act; it gives itself 30 days to say an application is complete and 120 days to decide, per The Crypto Times.
The NBA named Kalshi and Polymarket its prediction market exchanges and signed an integrity agreement with the CFTC, per crypto.news.
State fights continue: Utah sued Kalshi on 20 Oct, per crypto.news.
